questions.question_english:
The 'Pygmalion effect' in education refers to the phenomenon where higher expectations lead to improved performance. An emotionally intelligent Principal utilizes this by:
     (A) Publicly shaming low-performing teachers to motivate them to improve.
     (B) Communicating high expectations and genuine confidence in staff abilities.
     (C) Deliberately setting completely unachievable performance targets.
     (D) Deliberately ignoring staff workplace performance and instructional outcomes entirely.
options_english: Publicly shaming low-performing teachers during assembly to motivate them to improve.
Communicating high expectations and genuine confidence in staff abilities.
Deliberately setting completely unachievable performance targets to test staff physical endurance.
Deliberately ignoring staff workplace performance and instructional outcomes entirely.
questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is (B) because the Pygmalion effect illustrates that higher expectations from leaders can lead to enhanced performance among staff. An emotionally intelligent principal effectively leverages this by expressing genuine confidence in their staff's abilities and setting high expectations, which encourages educators to strive for excellence. Option (A) is incorrect as publicly shaming teachers is counterproductive and demotivating. Option (C) is also incorrect because setting unachievable targets can lead to frustration rather than improvement. Option (D) is wrong as ignoring performance outcomes does not foster a supportive environment for growth.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (b) है। पिग्मेलियन प्रभाव यह दर्शाता है कि नेताओं की उच्च अपेक्षाएँ स्टाफ के प्रदर्शन को बढ़ा सकती हैं। एक भावनात्मक रूप से बुद्धिमान प्रधानाचार्य इस प्रभाव का सही उपयोग करते हुए स्टाफ की क्षमताओं में वास्तविक आत्मविश्वास और उच्च अपेक्षाएँ संप्रेषित करते हैं, जिससे शिक्षकों को उत्कृष्टता के लिए प्रयास करने के लिए प्रेरित किया जाता है। विकल्प (A) गलत है क्योंकि शिक्षकों को सार्वजनिक रूप से शर्मिंदा करना प्रतिकूल और हतोत्साहित करने वाला है। विकल्प (C) भी गलत है क्योंकि असंभव लक्ष्यों को निर्धारित करना निराशा की ओर ले जा सकता है। विकल्प (D) गलत है क्योंकि प्रदर्शन परिणामों की अनदेखी करना विकास के लिए सहायक वातावरण नहीं बनाता।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Communicating high expectations and genuine confidence in staff abilities.
Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The Pygmalion effect demonstrates that higher leadership expectations lead to improved performance outcomes.

questions.question_english: Which of the following statements regarding Emotional Intelligence (EI) is incorrect?

questions.question_english: According to Reuven Bar-On’s model, Emotional-Social Intelligence is defined by:
options_english: The innate, genetically predetermined cognitive capacity to process complex mathematical logic and abstract reasoning
A fixed set of core personality traits and behavioral habits that cannot be altered or developed after adolescence
The cognitive capability to memorize, retain, and recall formal societal rules, administrative regulations, and social protocols
A set of emotional and social competencies that influence how effectively we understand and express ourselves
questions.explanation_english: The correct option is 'A set of emotional and social competencies that influence how effectively we understand and express ourselves'. Reuven Bar-On’s model defines emotional-social intelligence as a cross-section of interrelated emotional and social competencies, skills, and facilitators. This model posits that these competencies influence how effectively individuals understand and express themselves, relate to others, and cope with daily environmental demands and situational pressures throughout their personal and professional lives. The other options describe cognitive abilities or fixed personality traits, which do not align with the concept of emotional-social intelligence as defined by Bar-On.
